This issue might be a duplicate of (or closely related to) existing issues. Please check:
- #44291: MCP servers fail to connect when session starts during self-upgrade — same one-shot startup snapshot / no-reconnect behavior (already referenced in your report)
- #38266: local stdio MCP connection silently dropped mid-session, tools become permanently unavailable — same lack of reconnect path
- #35285: Desktop can keep stale local MCP state until full relaunch — same stale-state-on-startup pattern

If any of these fully cover your report, a maintainer may close this as a duplicate. Otherwise, the distinctions you've described (cold-start race with 14+ concurrent servers, per-server timeout budget exhaustion) are worth keeping as a separate feature request.
the similar issue is already there: #48741

Checked the three referenced issues — neither fully covers this report, so keeping this open as a separate feature request:

- **#38266** is a *mid-session* drop: local stdio MCP connections work at start, then silently die after some tool calls (transient `listTools()` failure permanently evicts the client). Our report is the opposite failure point — **all local MCPs are already marked failed at session start**, before any tool call, from the concurrent cold-start race.
- **#35285** is *stale state*: MCP works initially, then new Desktop sessions inherit a broken sidecar/MCP state until a full relaunch. Again, start works there; ours never starts.
- **#44291** is the closest (one-shot startup snapshot, no reconnect) but covers the self-upgrade timing, not the general cold-start race, and requests no warm-up mechanism.

What this report adds that none of them request: an **official warm-up / pre-spawn mechanism** (`mcp.warmup`-style knob) so session-start MCP spawn succeeds against 14+ concurrent local servers, plus surfacing the shared sidecar init budget. Happy to consolidate into whichever issue the maintainers prefer — but the warm-up half is not requested anywhere else.

## Update (v1.18.30, 2026-09-12) — full-day clean session log; proposing re-evaluation / closure

Same environment (Ubuntu 24.04 / WSL2, `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`). Note: the log rotated, so the current file covers **2026-09-12 only**; historical trend data beyond that is no longer locally available (I'm adding daily archival on my side so future deltas survive rotation).

**Current evidence (v1.18.30, 3 sessions, `opencode/big-pickle`, main agents plan/build/compaction):**

| Signature | Today (2026-09-12) |
|---|---|
| `message="stream error"` | **0** |
| socket_closed / Internal server error / Rate limit / Cannot connect | **0** |
| `Failed to fetch models.dev` (catalog) | **0** |
| `error=Aborted` | **2** — both immediately preceded by explicit `message=cancel` (user-initiated Esc), **not** silent drops |

274 `stream` calls vs 1,568 tool/permission events → healthy tool interleaving (no sustained no-op bursts).

**Version note:** `v1.18.27` added "Default streamed chunk timeouts to five minutes", which addresses the silent-stall variant this issue overlapped with (#37580/#38644 class).

**Proposal:** the socket/silent-drop class shows no recurrence on the current build. If no regression appears in the coming days, recommend closing as resolved on current stack. The remaining behavior class (text-only narration loop with **clean** logs, no transport errors, reproducible on 2026-08-28) is the discriminator we documented and is tracked separately in #46030.

## Update (v1.18.30, 2026-09-12) — no sustained narration-loop bursts observed today; loop-guard ask still open

Same environment, today's full-day log (3 sessions, `opencode/big-pickle`, main agents):

- **274 `stream` calls ↔ 1,568 tool/permission events** → healthy tool interleaving; no pure-narration signature.
- Peak minutes 10–12 streams/min, **isolated** (not the sustained 4-min bursts at up to 10/min seen on 2026-08-28, run `a9c7879c`).
- `error=Aborted`: 2, both preceded by `message=cancel` (user cancels).
- **Zero** transport errors (`stream error`/rate-limit/cannot-connect) — consistent with the discriminator I documented in this thread: the loop failure produces clean logs, so today's data doesn't confirm or deny the loop; it just shows no burst occurred.

**The loop-guard ask remains unanswered and stands:** detect N consecutive assistant turns that return a **text-only part (no tool call, no final answer)** and stop/surface a warning, mirroring the existing repeated-tool-call protection (#45442). A `no-tool-part` log signal would make this countable (like the stream-error buckets).

**Suggestion:** keep open until a loop guard lands or maintainer triage decides it should move to a feature request. I'll re-run the burst detector after any loop-side patch and report delta.

## Update (v1.18.30, 2026-09-12) — Internal-server-error class: no recurrence on the current build

Same environment as my evidence (Ubuntu 24.04/WSL2, `opencode/big-pickle`, no custom provider options). Today's full-day log:

- `AI_APICallError: Internal server error` (stream): **0** (was 172 on peak day 2026-07-24, ~409 cumulative per my 2026-08-11 evidence, then 890 total `stream error` across log history per my 2026-09-02 analysis).
- Total `message="stream error"` today: **0**.
- `v1.18.27` now defaults streamed chunk timeouts to five minutes (directly addresses the silent-stall variant of #37580 that this issue overlapped with).

**Proposal:** given zero recurrence on v1.18.30 plus the 1.18.27 timeout default, this class looks addressed and/or backend-stabilized. Suggest closing, or folding any remaining verification into #42950 (canonical for the stream-failure family). I'll report back if the 500s resurface.

+1 — adding a Desktop-side use case that strengthens this.

On OpenCode Desktop (Electron sidecar, v1.18.30), sessions are resumed via continue/resume so the *message history* survives — but there is no session-scoped *memory* mechanism: decisions, learned conventions, and task state from an earlier session do not re-enter context unless you manually paste them. We end up hand-rolling per-session memory via external tools (session transcript search + compact-to-knowledge-files) — which works, but it's exactly the gap this proposal (`--memory-file` / `memory` config) would close natively.

The proposed shape fits Desktop well too:

- Startup: inject the previous session summary as system context (or make it available to the session's first turn)
- End: append an auto-generated session summary to the memory file
- Config-side (`memory.file` + `autoSave`) is preferable to a CLI flag for Desktop users, since the desktop app doesn't expose CLI flags — so if both land, the config option is the one Desktop can actually use.

Also related: #48497 (long-term persistence memory system with /teach /recall /learn /memory commands) and #41453 (persistent session daemon + zero-tool-call recall) — a session-scoped layer (this issue) composes cleanly with both: long-term/global memory answers "who is the user", session memory answers "what happened in this session".

Hi all — I'm on the engineering side at OfoxAI. We reproduced this against our gateway with a real opencode client and a passthrough capture in front of the proxy, as suggested above. Findings:

**1. We can't reproduce with the config as posted.**
`baseURL: https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic` (no `/v1`) makes `@ai-sdk/anthropic` POST to `/anthropic/messages`, which returns 401/404 on our gateway today, so it produces no completions at all. The 80 requests in the screenshot must have come from a different config — please share the exact one. Note that `ofox` is a built-in provider in models.dev with Claude models already on `@ai-sdk/anthropic` + `https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic/v1`, so no custom provider is needed.

**2. With the correct base URL, opencode's marks reach us and are honored.**
opencode 1.18.30, custom provider with `@ai-sdk/anthropic`, ~28k-char `instructions` file, 10 tools, streaming. Captured bodies carry `cache_control` on `system[0]` and on the last two message blocks. Same session, three turns:

| turn | cache_creation_input_tokens | cache_read_input_tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 16784 | 0 |
| 2 | 16801 | 0 |
| 3 | 36 | 16784 |

Turn 3 reads exactly what turn 1 wrote. opencode's own recorded token counts match the captured responses.

On "proxy-side numbers can't be trusted": on our gateway they are billing numbers. Cache reads are billed at the discounted rate, so a read we report but didn't get upstream is a cost we absorb, not a number we'd inflate. We also don't inject breakpoints: a request with no `cache_control` returns 0/0, and the same request with a mark on `system` creates on the first call and reads on the second. Marks pass through unchanged in both directions. The reporter's own direct-SDK test against our gateway (1081 created, then 1081 read) shows the same thing. So the 0 in the August screenshot means we billed those turns as plain input — the numbers were accurate, and the open question is only why no mark was honored on that route at that time.

**3. The turn-2 miss is client-side, and probably worth its own issue.**
Byte-diffing the turn-1 and turn-2 system prompts, the only difference is a `<skill><location>` line: the same skill exists in `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.opencode/skills` and `~/.claude/skills` on this machine, and opencode picks a different path on each turn. That changes the system prefix every turn, so the cache is rewritten instead of read. Users with duplicated skill directories would see very low hit rates regardless of provider. Happy to open a separate issue with the diff if maintainers want it.

**4. What we can't verify.**
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5` has since been retired on our side (503, no provider), so the exact route the reporter hit in August can't be re-tested from outside.

@shaaaalllli97-alt @seven7763 — the capture above was against a different gateway, so nothing has been measured against ours yet. If either of you wants to run your passthrough against api.ofox.ai directly, we'll provide test credits: email hi@ofox.ai and mention this issue.

@utadamaaya — two asks: (a) retry with `baseURL: https://api.ofox.ai/anthropic/v1` (or the built-in `ofox` provider) and check whether turn 1 now shows `cache_creation_input_tokens > 0`; (b) if you're willing, email hi@ofox.ai with your account email so we can look at the usage details on our side for that period. Anything we find, we'll post here.

On the duplicate hint: #48508 is probably the same family, but the report does not confirm it.

Their directory is `C:\projects\my_svn_project`. On Windows `path.relative("/", "C:/projects/x")` is correct as long as the process runs from `C:`; it only returns an absolute path when the current process drive is a different one. So the symptom there needs either a non-`C:` directory or a process started from another drive.

If the #48508 reporter can run:

```sql
SELECT id, path, directory FROM session WHERE project_id = 'global' AND path LIKE '_:/%';
```

and gets rows back, then it is this bug and the migration in #48772 repairs them. If it comes back empty, the cause is elsewhere — likely the `workspace_id IS NULL` part of their report, which this does not touch.

Bumping this — it's still the right fix, and it's more urgent than when it was filed. Credit for the approach goes to **@0byte-coding** (original #33246); it had gone `dirty` against `dev`, so I ported it forward and validated it in production.

**Why it's urgent.** The system prompt is rebuilt on *every* request — `instruction.system()` re-reads the instruction files (`AGENTS.md`, `memory.md`), and `system.ts` injects `Today's date`. Any change to that prefix — editing an instruction file mid-session, or the date rolling over at midnight — makes the cached prefix diverge at token ~0 and forces a **full re-prefill of the entire conversation**. On a long agent session (we run a 1M-context DeepSeek V4 Flash via an OpenAI-compatible local server) that's ~450K tokens re-prefilled, ~4 minutes, with **no signal in the UI** — it just looks like the model is thinking. This is not Anthropic-specific; it hits every provider. The date variant is guaranteed once a day for any session that spans midnight.

Evidence: two consecutive requests with byte-identical `tools` and identical messages but a **different system-message hash** → 0 cached tokens → ~450K re-prefill. #29584 reports this exactly (auto-closed as stale); see also #36483 and #43722.

**Fix + validation.** Freeze the environment + instruction + MCP system parts once per session (on the first LLM call) and reuse them for the session's lifetime, keeping skills fresh. Rebased onto current `dev`, now open as **#48777**:

- PR: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/48777
- branch `fix/system-prompt-immutable` on `Capicua25x/opencode`; commit https://github.com/Capicua25x/opencode/commit/00d0a710e — co-authored by @0byte-coding, touches **only** `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts` (+26/−10)
- deployed and dogfooded: after the freeze, **editing `memory.md` mid-session no longer causes a prefill**, and the midnight rollover no longer does either

(#47816 handles the date-only case; this is the general fix.)

Same root cause on Windows — this appears to be the cross-platform version of #36671.

**Environment (Windows):**
- Windows 11 (10.0.26200), Alacritty 0.17.0, zellij-windows fork 0.43.1-win32.5 (WinGet)
- opencode 1.18.30 (npm), PowerShell 7

**Observed on `/exit` and Ctrl+C** (non-deterministic across runs):
1. The whole Zellij session closes (only pane dies → session exits) — `Bye Zellij!!`
2. Only opencode closes; pane stays alive and usable (correct case)
3. The pane is left in a corrupted terminal state (leaked alternate screen / raw mode): stray characters appear "as if the terminal were available when it is not", and keypresses/mouse moves print raw escape/mouse-report sequences until the pane is force-closed

Also confirmed on the macOS signal-broadcast path there is a related ConPTY-state leak: when the process dies without restoring terminal state, the pane keeps raw mode/altscreen (fingerprint of the same kill-everything cleanup interrupting the renderer's state restore).

Still reproducible on **1.18.30** (Windows, `"lsp": true`): the `.jsonc` entry named in this issue is still missing from `LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS`, and the effect is silence, not an error.

## Mechanism

`.jsonc` is absent from `LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS`, so the `didOpen` `languageId` falls back to `"plaintext"`. Biome's built-in server *does* list `.jsonc` in its `extensions` (so opencode routes the file to Biome), but Biome emits no diagnostics for `languageId: "plaintext"` — the file silently skips diagnostics.

Source at `dev`:

- `packages/opencode/src/lsp/language.ts:1` — `export const LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS: Record<string, string> = {`
- `packages/opencode/src/lsp/language.ts:53` — `".json": "json",` — and **no `.jsonc` key anywhere in the map**
- `packages/opencode/src/lsp/client.ts:560` — `const languageId = LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS[extension] ?? "plaintext"`

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set `"lsp": true` in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`.
2. Create a directory that contains a Biome root marker (e.g. `package-lock.json`).
3. Write two files with **identical** bytes — `broken.json` and `broken.jsonc`:

```json
{
  "a": 1,
  "b":
}
```

4. Write each and read the tool result's `<diagnostics>` block.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** both `.json` and `.jsonc` report the parse error.
**Actual:** only `.json` reports; `.jsonc` produces no diagnostics for that file.

Verbatim tool output after writing `broken.json`:

```
LSP errors detected in this file, please fix:
<diagnostics file="...\jsonc-bug-probe\broken.json">
ERROR [4:1] Expected an array, an object, or a literal but instead found '}'.
</diagnostics>
```

Writing `broken.jsonc` (same bytes, same directory) produced **no** `<diagnostics>` block for it.

Independent check that the server *can* parse it: the same `.jsonc` bytes report `error[biome] (parse) at 4:0: Expected an array, an object, or a literal but instead found '}'.` when routed through oh-my-openagent's own `lsp_diagnostics` path — so Biome handles `.jsonc`; only opencode's `languageId` is wrong.

## Proposed fix

Add the missing entries to `LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS`, at minimum:

```ts
".jsonc": "jsonc",
```

plus the other omissions already listed in this issue (`.toml`, `.mdx`, `.pyi`, `.h/.hpp/.hh/.hxx/.h++`, `.R`, and the bare `makefile` key).

Fresh Windows repro on **1.18.30**: the published `opencode.ai/config.json` produces **zero** diagnostics in the standard JSON language server, even when explicitly enabling validation — so unknown keys in `opencode.jsonc`/`omo.jsonc` are never caught (no VS-Code-style squiggles).

## Environment

```
opencode 1.18.30 (Windows 11)
plugins: oh-my-openagent 4.19.4, @cortexkit/opencode-antigravity-auth 2.2.1
lsp (in ~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc):
  "global-json-schema": {
    "command": ["cmd", "/c", "vscode-json-language-server", "--stdio"],
    "extensions": [".json", ".jsonc"],
    "initialization": { "json": { "validate": { "enable": true } } }
  }
server binary: vscode-json-language-server (vscode-langservers-extracted@4.10.0)
```

## Repro

1. Create a directory with **no** repo markers (no lockfile/biome.json).
2. `probe.json`:
   ```json
   {"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json","bogusKey":1}
   ```
3. Write it through opencode and read the write tool result's `<diagnostics>`.

## Expected vs actual

**Expected:** a schema violation for `bogusKey` (`Additional properties are not allowed ('bogusKey' was unexpected)`), i.e. the same squiggle VS Code shows.

**Actual:** no diagnostics block for `probe.json` at all. Verified twice (two separate writes, server warm). The same directory *does* produce diagnostics for other servers, so the LSP pipeline itself works:

```
# control — same bare dir, same session:
<diagnostics file="...\global-lsp-probe\probe2.py">
ERROR [1:6] "(" was not closed
...
```
```
# probe.json → nothing
```

## Mechanism

The published schema's **root is a `$ref` into top-level `$defs`**:

```json
{ "$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema",
  "$ref": "#/$defs/Config",
  "$defs": { "Config": { ... }, ... } }
```

`vscode-json-language-server` (and neovim `jsonls`) resolve a document's schema from its `$schema` URI but do not dereference a bare top-level `$ref` + `$defs` the way ajv/opencode's own validator does, so the document ends up with no effective schema and no diagnostics. That matches the report in this issue; the fresh part here is that it also fails with `json.validate.enable: true` and the exact VS Code server, not just neovim.

Suggested fix direction: publish the schema with `$defs` inlined (or wrap it as `{"type":"object","properties":{...}}` with no top-level `$ref`), or serve a JSON-LS-compatible variant at a documented secondary URL.

---

Note (separate, already tracked elsewhere): `.jsonc` additionally never reaches the server with the right languageId because `.jsonc` is missing from `LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS` (`packages/opencode/src/lsp/language.ts:53` has `".json": "json"`, no `.jsonc`; `client.ts:560` falls back to `"plaintext"`). **#41218 is a parse-duration problem.** A slow server (clangd, ~20s on a huge TU) exceeds the hardcoded 5s document / 10s full waits (`client.ts`), so the client gives up first. Its fix is configurable per-server timeouts.

**This issue is an initialization race.** Even an *instant* server (biome, parses in milliseconds) reports nothing on the FIRST write after cold start, then reports everything — including the first file under "other files" — on the next write seconds later (verbatim outputs in the body). Waiting longer cannot fix it, because the write path has already returned; the configurable timeouts proposed in #41218 change nothing here. What is needed is on the write path: surface the transient state (e.g. "server still starting") instead of rendering an empty result that reads as clean.

**#40413 is an initialization failure** (rust-analyzer never loads the nested workspace) surfaced as empty results — a server that never starts, versus a server that started but whose first request resolved before any diagnostics existed.

Three distinct failure points, three distinct fixes:
- #41218 → configurable waits (slow parse)
- #40413 → surface init errors instead of `[]` (never started)
- this issue → surface first-request transience on the write path (cold start)

I reproduced a focused child-session variant several times with `reflective-problem-solver` subagents:

1. I start the TUI with `opencode --auto`.
2. I spawn a foreground subagent and navigate to its child session.
3. The child requests permission for a trivial read-only shell command, such as:

   ```bash
   sed -n '95,126p' SKILL.md
   ```

4. The tool is shown and persisted as `running`, but I see:
   - no shell process being spawned;
   - no `spawning process` entry in the server log;
   - the command remaining blocked beyond its declared 60-second timeout.
5. I navigate **child → parent → reopen the same child** using the TUI parent/subagent navigation.
6. The permission is then auto-approved and execution continues.

When I restarted the client without `--auto`, I could see the underlying request in the parent TUI:

```text
△ Permission required
$ cd ... && sed -n '75,126p' SKILL.md
```

The API also confirmed that the request belonged to the child session:

```json
{
  "action": "shell",
  "resources": ["sed -n '95,126p' SKILL.md"],
  "source": {
    "type": "tool",
    "messageID": "msg_099d9ac07001TkB5bCeu1YU30r",
    "id": "toolu_019PrGvAuZ68p1zcLqosynuH"
  }
}
```

I saw this in three separate child sessions. Equivalent commands complete immediately when I run them directly.

From tracing the TUI, the navigation handlers only change the local route. Re-entering a session remounts its frame and runs:

```ts
data.session.sync(sessionID, { children: true })
data.session.permission.sync(sessionID)
data.session.form.sync(sessionID)
```

My best reading is that auto-approval does not reliably observe a child permission request until the route is remounted and its permission state is synchronized again.

There also seems to be a related UX issue: a tool waiting for permission is projected as `running`, even though execution has not reached the process spawner. The shell timeout starts only after spawn/registration, so it does not terminate this permission wait.

I hope these details help narrow it down. I can collect a before/after API capture around the navigation sequence if that would be useful.
